analysis: Examined both test-guide revisions and SSD-reference metadata/patch. docs/developer/test.md head:177-203 adds an opt-in shared-engine restore-contention benchmark using an isolated ephemeral cache and foreign-tenant prefill/donor workloads; existing isolation, encryption, refusal and qualification caveats remain. docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md head:119 documents provider-staged imports using zeroed host-backed destinations without eval/stream fences, avoiding the process-wide evalLock, with up to one 64 MiB transient host source outside the MLX allocator. No concrete security regression is established by these documentation changes alone. Relevant boundaries/assets are TB-007, A-001 and T-041 (tenant/cache isolation and timing), T-028 (residual data), and T-010 (retirement/cancellation). Next pass must examine CheckpointHostZeros.swift, CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift, PagedCheckpointStorage.swift and CompleteCheckpointImportPlan.swift for initialized-buffer readiness, copy/source lifetime, bounded aggregate host-memory admission, concurrent imports and cancellation cleanup. Review their interactions with SSDHybridCheckpointStore read admission, native adoption/ownership and the new ModelCheckpointRestoreContentionLiveTests.swift; restored-token and relative-TTFT assertions do not independently prove tenant isolation or resource bounds. Implementations and unchanged callers are not supplied, so the documented allocation/fence behavior cannot be validated here. No visible changes to authorization, attestation, transport encryption or billing contracts.
